Interactively tie a proxy record to an astronomical solution (random order, tie and untie, inspect)

Source: R/astro_anchor_interactive.R
astro_anchor_interactive.Rd

A more flexible alternative to astro_anchor. The proxy record (top) and the astronomical solution (bottom) are shown in one window with their peaks (or troughs). Tie points can be set, removed and changed in any order: click a peak of the proxy record and then a peak of the astronomical solution to tie them (or first the astronomical peak and then the proxy peak); click a tied peak again to untie it. The windows can be zoomed and moved with the buttons above the plot, so that long records can be tied piece by piece. Press Tune and inspect at any moment: a second window shows the record tuned to the current tie points together with a cycle extracted from it, the astronomical solution and the sedimentation rate between the tie points, so that the result can be judged while tie points are still being added or removed.

Usage

astro_anchor_interactive(
  astro_solution = NULL,
  proxy_signal = NULL,
  proxy_min_or_max = "max",
  astrosolution_min_or_max = "max",
  pts = 3,
  ties = NULL,
  time_dir = TRUE,
  peaks_in_view = 12,
  inspect_period = NULL,
  inspect_band = 0.25,
  sedrate_factor = 1,
  inspect_wavelet = FALSE,
  locator_fun = NULL
)

Arguments

astro_solution

Astronomical solution to tie to (matrix or data frame with two columns: time/age (e.g. kyr) in column 1, value in column 2; rows with NA are removed and rows are sorted on column 1). Required, no default (Default=NULL gives an error).

proxy_signal

Proxy record to be tied (matrix or data frame with two columns: depth/time in column 1, proxy value in column 2; rows with NA are removed). Use extract_signal first if a single cycle of the record should be tied. Required, no default (Default=NULL gives an error).

proxy_min_or_max

Tie the maxima or the minima of the proxy record (character): "max" or "min". Default="max".

astrosolution_min_or_max

Tie the maxima or the minima of the astronomical solution (character): "max" or "min". Default="max".

pts

Number of points to the left and right of a value that the peak detection (max_detect, min_detect) compares it with (integer, >= 1); larger values give fewer, more certain peaks. Default=3.

ties

Existing tie points to start from (data frame with the columns data_x (proxy depth/time) and insolation_x (astronomical age), otherwise the first two columns are used; e.g. the output of astro_anchor). They are snapped to the nearest peaks. NULL starts without tie points. Default=NULL.

time_dir

Direction of time in the proxy record (logical): TRUE if time increases with increasing depth/time values, FALSE if it decreases (the proxy axis is then reversed). Default=TRUE.

peaks_in_view

Approximate number of peaks shown in each window at the start (numeric, > 0). Default=12.

inspect_period

Period of the cycle extracted from the tuned record in the inspection window, in the time unit of the astronomical solution (numeric, > 0); NULL uses the median spacing of the peaks of the astronomical solution. Default=NULL.

inspect_band

Relative half-width of the extracted band (numeric, between 0 and 1): 0.25 extracts 0.75 to 1.25 times inspect_period. Default=0.25.

sedrate_factor

Factor applied to the sedimentation rate (depth units per time unit) shown in the inspection window (numeric, > 0), for example 100 to go from m/kyr to cm/kyr. Default=1.

inspect_wavelet

Also show the wavelet scalogram of the tuned record in the inspection window at the start (logical, TRUE or FALSE); it can be switched on and off with the Wavelet button. Default=FALSE.

locator_fun

Function without arguments that returns the next mouse click in normalised device coordinates as a list with x and y, like locator(1); returning NULL finishes. NULL uses graphics::locator(1). Another function (for example one that replays a list of clicks) allows scripted use and testing. When no interactive device is available and ties is given, the snapped tie points are returned without opening a window. Default=NULL.

Value

A data frame with the tie points sorted by depth/time: data_x, data_y (proxy), insolation_x, insolation_y (astronomical solution).

Details

Buttons (click them with the left mouse button): Tune and inspect (open or update the inspection window), Undo (remove the last change), Clear (remove all tie points), Zoom +/Zoom - (both windows), P <, P > (move the proxy window), A <, A > (move the astronomical window), Fit (show the whole records), Sync (move the astronomical window to the partners of the tie points in the proxy window, or the other way round if there are none), Wavelet (switch the wavelet scalogram of the tuned record in the inspection window on or off) and Done. A right click also finishes. Tie points that are in the wrong order (the tuned time would run backwards) are drawn in orange, and the tuning refuses to run until they are fixed.

The result has the same four columns as the output of astro_anchor and can be used directly by plot_astro_anchor and anchor2time.

See also

astro_anchor, plot_astro_anchor, anchor2time

Examples

# \donttest{
# Tie points can be given as a starting point and are snapped to the nearest peaks;
# without an interactive graphics device (as here) they are returned as they are.
astrosignal <- na.omit(astrosignal_example)
tie_start <- data.frame(data_x = c(155, 160, 165), insolation_x = c(5040, 5400, 5560))
proxy <- grey[grey[, 1] < 175, ]
ties <- astro_anchor_interactive(astro_solution = astrosignal,
                                 proxy_signal = proxy,
                                 ties = tie_start)
ties
#>   data_x   data_y insolation_x insolation_y
#> 1 155.04 362.4783         5036    1.0902778
#> 2 160.01 380.1990         5393    0.6553615
#> 3 164.99 426.3102         5550    2.1563294
# in an interactive session, leave out 'ties' to tie the peaks with the mouse
# }
